title: Standard Deviation: Ungrouped and Grouped Data
seo_title: Sec 4 Standard deviation Worksheets: Free Secondary 4 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: range, interquartile range and standard deviation as measures of spread; calculation of the standard deviation for a set of data (grouped and ungrouped); using the mean and standard deviation to compare two sets of data
meta_desc: Free Secondary 4 maths worksheets on standard deviation: lists of data, Σx and Σx² formulas, grouped data with mid-values, transformations and comparing data sets with mean and SD. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: SD = √(Σx²/n − x̄²): it measures spread about the mean.
key_sub: Higher mean = better on average; smaller SD = more consistent.
body_html:
How it works

  • The standard deviation measures how spread out the data is from the mean.
  • SD = √(Σ(x − x̄)² ÷ n) = √(Σx² ÷ n − x̄²).
  • For grouped data, use the mid-value of each class: SD = √(Σfx² ÷ Σf − x̄²).
  • Adding a constant to every value does not change the SD; multiplying every value by k multiplies the SD by k.
  • To compare data sets: a higher mean is better on average; a smaller SD is more consistent.
Example

Find the SD of 2, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 7, 9.

Mean = 40 ÷ 8 = 5

Σ(x − 5)² = 32

√(32 ÷ 8)

Answer: 2

Example

For 10 values, Σx = 50 and Σx² = 340. Find the SD.

Mean = 5

√(340 ÷ 10 − 5²) = √9

Answer: 3

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting the square root (that gives the variance).
  • Dividing by n − 1 or forgetting to divide by n.
  • Using class boundaries instead of mid-values for grouped data.
  • Thinking that adding a number to every value changes the standard deviation.

faq.q: What does the standard deviation tell you?
faq.a: How far, on average, the values are from the mean. A small SD means the data is close together; a large SD means it is spread out.
SD = √(Σx²/n − x̄²) is quickest when you are given Σx and Σx², or when using a calculator. For grouped data use Σfx² and Σf with mid-values.

faq.q: What happens to the SD if I add 5 to every value?
faq.a: Nothing. The whole data set shifts, but the spread stays the same. Only the mean increases by 5.

faq.q: How do I compare two data sets?
faq.a: Use the mean to compare the average and the standard deviation to compare consistency. The smaller SD is more consistent.

sets.title: Adding to or multiplying every value

items.q: A data set has mean 50 and standard deviation 1.5. Every value is multiplied by 2. What is the new standard deviation?
items.e: Multiplying every value by 2 multiplies the spread by 2: 1.5 × 2 = 3.

items.q: A set of marks has mean 47 and standard deviation 2. Every mark is increased by 3. What are the new mean and standard deviation?
items.e: Adding the same amount for every value moves the mean by 3 but does not change the spread: mean 50, SD 2.

items.q: Values with mean 75 and standard deviation 3 are each multiplied by 2 and then increased by 10. What are the new mean and standard deviation?
items.e: Mean: 75 × 2 + 10 = 160. SD: only the multiplication matters, 3 × 2 = 6. mean 160, SD 6.

items.q: Values with mean 78 and standard deviation 2.5 are each multiplied by 2 and then increased by 5. What are the new mean and standard deviation?
